back: Reverse sits in front of servers (hides servers from clients). Forward sits in front of clients (hides clients from servers).

front: Five common roles of a reverse proxy?
back: TLS termination, load balancing, caching, compression, and static file serving. Also: rate limiting, request routing, response buffering.
A load balancer distributes traffic. A reverse proxy may also load-balance, but adds TLS termination, caching, compression, buffering and routing. Many tools do both.
Terminating TLS at the reverse proxy. Traffic to backends is plain HTTP. Centralises cert management and frees app server CPU.
The proxy reads the backend's response quickly, frees the backend connection, then streams to the (possibly slow) client. Backend handles more concurrent requests.
Both compress text (HTML, CSS, JS, JSON). Brotli achieves better ratios but is slower at high levels. Most proxies use moderate Brotli (level 4–6).
A widely-used open-source reverse proxy and web server. Efficient at static file serving, TLS termination, compression and load balancing.
A modern reverse proxy (CNCF project, created at Lyft). Designed for microservices: supports HTTP/2, gRPC, retries, circuit breaking, tracing, and integrates with service meshes.
A small proxy deployed alongside each service instance. Handles mTLS, retries, circuit breaking and tracing without application code changes.
A control plane (Istio, Linkerd) managing sidecar proxies across all services. Provides uniform security, observability and traffic control.

front: When is a service mesh worth it?
back: Large microservice deployments (dozens+ services, multiple teams). Too much complexity for small setups.
A reverse proxy that manages external access to services in a Kubernetes cluster, handling TLS, routing, and virtual hosting.

front: Without a buffering proxy, how long does a 200 KB response hold a worker for a 50 KB/s client?
back: About 4 s, even though the real work took 20 ms. With buffering the worker is free in ~20 ms.
Opening many connections and trickling data very slowly to tie up every server worker; a buffering, event-driven proxy absorbs it.

front: When must you turn proxy buffering off?
back: For streaming responses: server-sent events, long polling, large downloads, streamed LLM tokens.
